costs_config.blocking_note: Every value above is an UNSOURCED PLACEHOLDER of the right order of magnitude. It exists so the cost machinery is exercised and hash-tracked, NOT so cost numbers can be quoted. Because a 0.20 pp TER delta alone exceeds the 0.124 pp G1 gate, no cost-sensitive claim may be promoted until these are replaced with sourced values (KIID/PRIIPs for TER, provider factsheets for tracking difference, venue data for spreads). Phase 3 (R2E) must therefore treat TER as a SWEPT DIMENSION (0/10/20/30 bp) rather than reading these point values.

data_policy.core_principle: reproducibility != redistribution. A licensed dataset can be used reproducibly if the repository carries complete provenance and a content hash, so that a second party holding the same legitimate source can verify byte equality. Open redistribution remains a valuable property, but it must not be equated with data existence or with scientific reproducibility.

availability_status.meaning: Whether the series can be obtained at all, and on what terms.

redistribution_status.meaning: Whether the raw bytes may be republished from this repository.

reproducibility_status.meaning: Whether a second party can reconstruct the identical input. LICENSED_REPRODUCIBLE requires complete provenance plus a SHA-256 that a holder of the same licensed source can check byte-for-byte.

licensed_data_pathway.verification_contract: A second user with the same legitimate source recomputes the local file hash and compares it against the recorded expected_sha256. Equality establishes that both parties calibrated from identical bytes.
licensed_data_pathway.what_this_is_not: This is not open-data reproducibility. It is licensed reproducibility, and must be labelled as such in every report.

extra.blocks_phase_5: gates.require_phase_pass refuses to start any phase whose predecessor acceptance is not PASS, so Phase 5 is blocked by default and this run does not lift that. Whether to proceed on the UNCALIBRATED_ASSUMPTION prior is an operator decision: PROJECT_META's PARTIAL branch contemplates Phases 5 and 6 running with the remaining satellites left INDETERMINATE_BY_CONSTRUCTION, but BLOCKED_NETWORK is not PARTIAL. Analytically the null tests and the mu-neutral gold claim are constructed to need no empirical mu, and their ceiling is MODEL_CONSISTENT_FINDING either way. What R3 blocks unconditionally is EMPIRICAL_SUPPORT, which only Engine A on real data can award.

blocked_by: Not verified locally: no file downloaded, no row counted, no hash computed in this environment. Teil D's 'CORE-Daten nicht verfuegbar -> STOP' is a finding about the world and needs reproducible evidence. Second-hand testimony, however careful, is not that.
candidate_verdict.critical_distinction: LICENCE_REQUIRED is not 'the data does not exist'. It exists and is commercially obtainable. What does not exist is a version this repository may redistribute. A FAIL on these grounds is a statement about the project's self-imposed open-reproducibility condition, NOT about the world's data.
candidate_verdict.if_the_condition_were_relaxed: If the operator accepts licensed data held outside the repository, or a documented open proxy with its own data_status, PARTIAL becomes reachable: GOLD now has an admissible open proxy (World Bank Pink Sheet, CC BY 4.0), and HICP and €STR are open. CORE remains the binding constraint either way.
candidate_verdict.reasoning: Round 2 answered the CORE question for the CORRECT index. FTSE All-World long history is a licensed LSEG product - the freely accessible Historic Index Values give roughly two years, and LSEG requires a licence for use and distribution. The Vanguard NAV fallback has only ~7 years (share class inception 2019-07-23) and is a fund series, not the benchmark. So no >=360-month CORE series is redistributable under this project's open-reproducibility condition. Under the revised taxonomy that is FAIL_ACCESS_CONSTRAINT, not FAIL_DATA_UNAVAILABLE: data_exists=true, data_acquired=false.
candidate_verdict.what_would_settle_it: One run with egress that fetches the LSEG Historic Index Values page and the FTSE All-World licence terms itself, and records the observed coverage. That is a small, cheap check - it does not require obtaining the data, only confirming it is not obtainable openly.

cost_sourcing.phase3_urgency: Phase 3 measured a 30 bp TER difference at 5,600 EUR of real terminal wealth over 20 years, exceeding the 5,000 EUR G1 materiality gate on its own. Sourcing these values is therefore a precondition for any cost-sensitive claim, not housekeeping.
cost_sourcing.reason_unmodified: No TER value could be retrieved from an authoritative document, so config/costs.json is unchanged and remains PLACEHOLDER_NOT_SOURCED. Writing TER values recalled from model training rather than read from a PRIIPs KID would produce numbers with no source URL, no retrieval date and no content hash - indistinguishable from the placeholders already there, but falsely dressed as sourced. PROJECT_META forbids exactly that.
cost_sourcing.tracking_difference_note: Tracking difference is not disclosed in a PRIIPs KID. It must be derived from published fund NAV history against the licensed index series, or taken from an issuer TD disclosure. Deriving it requires the index history, which is the same licence blocker as CORE.

specification_conflicts.conflict: B.5 was decided as option_b, fx=EXCLUDED_BY_DESIGN. The rationale recorded in config/fx.json is that asset processes are 'interpreted as EUR-denominated total returns with the FX component folded into their volatility'. Round 2 establishes that the CORE benchmark is FTSE All-World NET RETURN in USD, and that the fund's base currency is USD. A EUR-denominated CORE series is therefore not what would be calibrated from.
specification_conflicts.decision_owner: human operator - this is a B.5 first-class assumption, not an implementation detail
specification_conflicts.resolution: option_b retained but redefined as EXCLUDED_AS_SEPARATE_STOCHASTIC_FACTOR. No separate stochastic FX factor is simulated, preserving the original motivation. But every non-EUR calibration series MUST be converted to EUR before return estimation - data preprocessing, not a modelled process. Supported claims are limited to EUR-investor total-return behaviour; isolated FX risk, hedging decisions, FX forecasts and asset/currency decomposition are explicitly unsupported. See config/fx.json.
resolution_options: Switch B.5 to option_a and model an explicit EUR/USD process (adds the parameter uncertainty option_b was chosen to avoid).
Keep option_b but rewrite the rationale honestly: FX risk is OMITTED, not absorbed, and every CORE-derived number is a USD-investor number relabelled.
Source a natively EUR-denominated net-return series, which would make the original rationale true - but round 2 could not verify one exists openly.
specification_conflicts.scope_of_damage: Phases 1-3 are NOT invalidated: they run on an assumed prior, not on calibrated data, and the conflict bites only at calibration. But B.5 must be revisited BEFORE any calibrated run, and the rationale text in config/fx.json is inaccurate as written once a USD benchmark is in play.
specification_conflicts.why_it_matters: Calibrating CORE from a USD series leaves two options and both break the recorded B.5 rationale. (a) Convert USD->EUR with an FX series: that IS an FX process, which option_b excludes. (b) Treat USD returns as if they were EUR returns: that does not 'fold FX into volatility', it OMITS FX entirely, misstating both the mean and the variance faced by a EUR investor. The recorded rationale would only have been accurate for a natively EUR-denominated series.

effect_on_existing_results.reason: config/fx.json is not read by any numeric code path. Phases 1-3 run on an UNCALIBRATED_ASSUMPTION prior and load no historical series, so the calibration rule above has nothing to act on there. The conflict arises only at the transition to empirical calibration.

historical_calibration.classification: This is DATA PREPROCESSING, not a stochastic process. It happens once, before calibration, on observed history.
historical_calibration.fx_quote_convention: MUST be recorded per series in the data manifest. A quote-direction error silently inverts the currency effect and is not detectable from the numbers alone.
historical_calibration.level_form: I_EUR(t) = I_FOREIGN(t) * FX(t), with the FX quote convention documented explicitly per series
historical_calibration.rule: MANDATORY. Every non-EUR benchmark series MUST be converted into EUR BEFORE return estimation or calibration.

fx_config.mandatory_disclosure: This decision, including the supported and unsupported claim lists, MUST be restated in every result report, per B.5.
fx_config.revision_reason: The original formulation said non-EUR asset returns were 'interpreted as EUR-denominated total returns with the FX component folded into their volatility'. Phase 4 round 2 established that the CORE benchmark is FTSE All-World NET RETURN in USD. For a USD series that sentence is false: reading USD returns as EUR returns does not fold FX into volatility, it OMITS FX, misstating both the mean and the variance faced by a EUR investor. The error was in the interpretation clause, not in the decision to avoid a separate stochastic FX factor.

simulation.rationale: This preserves the original motivation for option_b: no future USD/EUR correlation has to be parameterised, so the parameter space does not expand into a dimension that G6-style underdetermination would make unestimable. What changes is that the calibration now measures the risk a EUR investor actually bears, instead of a USD investor's risk relabelled.
simulation.rule: Simulate the resulting EUR-denominated asset return process directly.

tax_config._spec_ref: PROJECT_META v3, Teil B.1-B.3. Every assumption carries an explicit legal_status.

abgeltungsteuer.assumption_note: 25% Abgeltungsteuer (§32d Abs.1 EStG) plus 5.5% Solidaritaetszuschlag on the tax amount. Soli is modelled as fully applicable to Kapitalertragsteuer (the 2021 Soli reduction does not extend to Abgeltungsteuer).

etc_debt_security_B3_alternative.assumption_note: Contrast variant reflecting BFH case law on §23 EStG private disposal transactions: tax-free after a one-year holding period. That case law concerns deliverable domestic constructions (Xetra-Gold), NOT this product. Computed only because B.3 requires both variants to be reported while legal_status != VERIFIED.

etc_debt_security_B3_assumed.assumption_note: IE00B4ND3602 is an Irish debt security (ETC) without a physical delivery claim. Assumed fully taxable under §20 EStG: no Teilfreistellung, no holding-period exemption. Effective ~26.375% on the gain.

b3_dual_reporting.materiality: ~26% on the gain versus 0% (alternative) - decides the GOLD claim on its own.
b3_dual_reporting.rule: While assets_tax_classes.etc_debt_security_B3_assumed.legal_status != VERIFIED, every GOLD claim MUST be computed and reported under BOTH variants. A single-variant GOLD result is not a valid deliverable.

basiszins.assumption_note: Assumption, to be checked against the annual BMF-Schreiben: 2023 ~2.55%, 2024 ~2.29%, 2025 ~2.53%, 2021/2022 negative -> floored to 0. The Basiszins is derived from the yield of long-dated German government bonds and is published at the start of each calendar year. Coupled to the modelled short rate so that an inflation regime cannot occur without a corresponding rise in the Basiszins (B.2 rationale: a deterministic Basiszins systematically understates the tax burden in inflationary worlds).

church_tax.assumption_note: §32d Abs.1 S.4-5 EStG. With q=0 and k=9%: effective 27.9951%. Sensitivity only per A.4; baseline is none.
church_tax.formula: est = (kapitalertrag - 4*q) / (4 + k_percent); total = est * (1 + soli + k)

freistellungsauftrag.assumption_note: Sparer-Pauschbetrag §20 Abs.9 EStG, 1000 EUR since 2023 (single filer). Modelled as nominally constant over the whole horizon - NOT indexed to inflation. This is a conservative, explicitly stated modelling choice: in a high-inflation world the real value of the FSA decays.

legal_status_vocabulary.NOT_IN_DECISION_PATH: Implemented and tested, but not exercised by any decision-path run. Must not gate.
legal_status_vocabulary.TO_BE_VERIFIED: Modelled assumption, plausible, NOT yet checked against primary source. Blocks promotion above MODEL_CONSISTENT_FINDING for any claim it materially drives.
legal_status_vocabulary.VERIFIED: Checked against primary legal source; citation recorded.

teilfreistellung.assumption_note: §20 InvStG: 30% partial exemption for private investors in equity funds (>=51% equity). Applied to both Vorabpauschale and realised gains.

vorabpauschale.assumption_note: §18 InvStG (Basisertrag = NAV_start_of_year * 0.7 * Basiszins, capped at the Wertsteigerung of the year, floored at 0, reduced by 1/12 per full month preceding the acquisition month) and §19 InvStG (accumulated Vorabpauschalen reduce the gain on disposal, preventing double taxation). An ETC is a debt security, not an Investmentfonds, so no Vorabpauschale applies to GOLD under either tax variant.

withholding_tax_credit.action: Code and hand-checks are retained and still execute in the test suite, but are DECOUPLED from every gate. No gate may depend on this branch.
withholding_tax_credit.known_v2_defect: The v2 implementation applied credit = min(swht, dt) against 26.375% rather than against 25% Einkommensteuer with Solidaritaetszuschlag applied afterwards. This is the defect that held R2 at FAIL_LEGAL_EXACTNESS. It is corrected in the retained code, but the correction is NOT a decision-path claim.
withholding_tax_credit.rationale: Accumulating Irish funds suffer foreign withholding tax at fund level; it is not creditable for the German private investor, and the Teilfreistellung is the statutory compensation mechanism. After DIVIDEND was reclassified to equity_fund, the universe contains no direct_stocks instrument, so no decision-path run exercises this branch.

unmodelled_boundary_conditions: Emergency fund, human capital, statutory/occupational pension, liquidity events and interim withdrawals are NOT modelled (B.6). This is a partial analysis of portfolio allocation, not financial planning.
